diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $\E[\bm Y| \XX]\in \col(\bm X)$ only if $f-f^*$ vanishes at $x_i$, i.e., $f\in V_n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The condition $\E[\bm Y|\XX]\in\col(\bm X)$ is equivalent to $f(x_i)=f^*(x_i)$ for all sample points $x_i$, i.e., $f$ agrees with an element of $V_n$ at the sampled points. This does not imply $f\in V_n$ globally. For example, a function that agrees with a constant at finitely many points need not be constant everywhere. Thus the stated equivalence with $f\in V_n$ is false.

failure_location.quote: Note that $\E[\bm Y| \XX]\in \col(\bm X)$ only if $f-f^*$ vanishes at $x_i$, i.e., $f\in V_n$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the phrase 'i.e., $f\in V_n$' by a correct statement such as 'i.e., $f$ agrees with an element of $V_n$ at the sampled points' or 'for instance, if $f\in V_n$'.
issues.overall_effect: This is an explanatory remark in Section 2. It does not invalidate any formal theorem or algorithm, but it misstates when the noiseless conditional mean lies in the column space and hence when the regression bias vanishes.
issues.title: False equivalence in bias condition for linear regression
issues.why_classification: The error is local to an explanatory prose claim, has no downstream formal consequences, and admits a one-sentence correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that if $|\supp_{\delta}(\bm q_n^{*})|>n(n+1)/2$, the corresponding $R_iR^\top_i, i\in\text{supp}_{\delta}(\bm q^{*}_n)$ are linearly dependent.

issues.failure_explanation: To perturb a feasible point of $\mathcal P_m(\delta)$ while preserving the simplex constraint $\|\bm q\|_1=1$, the perturbation direction $\bm a$ must also satisfy $\sum_i a_i=0$. The linear dependence of the matrices $R_iR_i^\top$ only yields a direction with $\sum_i a_i/\sigma^2(x_i)\,R_iR_i^\top=0$; it does not by itself imply $\sum_i a_i=0$. At an optimal point this additional property follows from the KKT conditions (the derivative of $H$ is constant on the support), but that argument is omitted. Hence the stated perturbation is not shown to remain feasible, and the support bound is not fully justified as written.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, there exists a direction $\bm a = (a_1, \ldots, a_m)^\top$ supported on $\text{supp}_{\delta}(\bm q^{*}_n)$ such that  $\sum_{i\in [m]}\frac{a_i}{\sigma^2(x_i)}R_iR^\top_i = 0$. Applying a perturbation argument for $\bm q^{*}_n$ along $\bm a$ yields another optimal solution that has a smaller $\delta$-support.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing KKT argument showing that any null direction of the matrix sum at an optimal point must have $\sum_i a_i=0$, so that the perturbation preserves the simplex constraint and reduces the support.
issues.overall_effect: The support-size bound in Lemma \ref{mkjh} lacks a complete proof. The result is standard and likely true, but the proof as written leaves a nontrivial feasibility step unaddressed. No downstream result is invalidated if the standard argument is supplied.
issues.title: Incomplete feasibility justification in support bound proof
issues.why_classification: The gap is a contained missing step in the proof of a standard support bound; the lemma's conclusion remains true with a short additional argument and no major result is lost.
